direct-election-head-of-state.reason: Direct, parliamentary and ceremonial arrangements all work in different democracies, so I don't think one method is clearly best.

central-bank-independence.reason: Insulating monetary policy from electoral cycles has a decent track record against inflation, though a narrow price mandate can neglect employment.

no-land-for-peace.reason: Historic attachment matters, but I think lives saved by a durable peace can justify territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.reason: I see property rights as having both independent moral weight and social limits, so 'only so far as' goes further than I would.

soviet-state-capitalist.reason: This turns on contested definitions of socialism within Marxist theory, and I would rather lay out the positions than pick one.

precautionary-principle.reason: When potential harms are serious or irreversible, waiting for certainty can be too late, though precaution should be proportionate.

collective-defense.reason: Credible mutual defense commitments seem to have deterred aggression effectively, even though they constrain national choice.

annexed-territory-occupation.reason: Letting time legitimize conquest rewards aggression, though I recognize very old cases get genuinely murky.

subordinate-church-to-state.reason: Religious bodies should obey general laws, but placing clergy under civil authority threatens freedom of religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.reason: A unifying figurehead has real value in some systems, while elected executive presidents legitimately lead partisan programs.

force-to-prevent-secession.reason: States have an interest in their integrity, but holding an unwilling population by force tends to bring grave harm.

region-keeps-system.reason: Federal and asymmetric arrangements show a region can keep distinct institutions while belonging to a larger state.

sacred-ruler.reason: I don't think political authority should rest on claims of divine descent; officeholders are ordinary people.

flat-income-tax.reason: Simplicity is appealing, but progressive rates better match ability to pay.

character-from-environment.reason: The evidence points to substantial contributions from both genes and environment, so neither 'mainly' claim fits well.

sovereign-above-law.reason: The rule of law means rulers are bound by the same laws as everyone else.

space-expansion.reason: Space exploration is worthwhile and may matter long term, but I wouldn't call it the central goal ahead of earthly problems.

mixed-constitution.reason: Spreading power across different bodies and checks seems more stable and safer than concentrating it in one.

leader-cult.reason: Glorifying a leader as the embodiment of the nation tends to erode accountability and feed authoritarianism.

equal-parenting.reason: Shared parenting is often good for children, but a firm presumption can fit badly in cases involving conflict or abuse.

class-struggle-under-socialism.reason: This is an internal question of Marxist doctrine where I don't hold a view of my own.

land-redistribution.reason: Land reform has sometimes reduced deep injustice, but expropriation without fair process has also caused famine and collapse.

refugee-return.reason: This is central to some of the most contested conflicts, and I would rather not take a side on a general rule.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.reason: Redrawing borders around ethnicity has repeatedly been a pretext for war and should not justify territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.reason: Freedom of conscience includes the freedom to leave one's religion without penalty.

women-must-cover.reason: The state should not impose religious dress codes on women.

common-currency.reason: Shared currencies ease trade but remove a tool for handling local shocks, so the answer depends on the countries involved.

kin-peoples-union.reason: Cultural ties among related peoples are fine, but pursuing political unity across borders on ancestry tends to be destabilizing.

national-cultural-autonomy.reason: Minority-run schools and cultural institutions can protect identity without requiring new states.

rights-where-you-live.reason: Equal rights at home is the ideal, but I can't fault persecuted people who decided they needed a refuge of their own.

material-conditions-drive-history.reason: Economic conditions matter a lot, but ideas, religion and moral movements also drive change independently.

ban-cartels.reason: Price-fixing cartels clearly harm consumers, and competition law is important, though breaking up firms should be case by case.

no-bailouts.reason: Moral hazard is real, but letting a systemic bank collapse can harm far more innocent people than a well-designed rescue.

courts-bound-by-majority.reason: Independent courts protecting rights against majorities are part of what makes a democracy liberal.

gender-parity-bodies.reason: Balanced representation is a good goal, and I'm unsure whether mandated quotas are the right means.

economic-self-sufficiency.reason: Closed autarkic blocs, especially built on colonies, impoverish people and have historically fueled conflict.

trade-labor-env-standards.reason: Binding standards help keep trade from rewarding abuse, though they must avoid becoming disguised protectionism.

moral-incentives.reason: Purpose and duty motivate people, but replacing pay as the main incentive has generally worked poorly.

armed-group-creates-revolution.reason: Historically, small armed vanguards acting without mass support mostly failed, and I don't endorse the violence it implies.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.reason: Legal privilege by birth conflicts with equal citizenship, though purely ceremonial titles do little harm.

history-own-civilization.reason: Starting from one's own country is natural, but students also need a real understanding of the wider world.

civilizing-tutelage.reason: The 'civilizing mission' rationale has justified domination and great harm, and no society has that right over another.

patriotic-education.reason: Schools should teach civic knowledge and appreciation, but instilling loyalty can become indoctrination.

end-racial-preferences.reason: This is a live, closely divided policy dispute where I prefer to present the arguments rather than take a side.

public-money-creation.reason: Bank lending under central bank regulation is workable, and full public money creation risks politicizing credit.

capitalism-adapts.reason: Market economies have repeatedly reformed and survived severe crises, though future adaptation isn't guaranteed.

former-empire-influence.reason: Ordinary ties are fine, but past imperial rule shouldn't give a country a special claim over its former territories.

delink-world-market.reason: The countries that grew fastest mostly integrated into world trade, though on terms they managed carefully.

labor-aristocracy.reason: Global inequality is real, but rich-country workers still face their own exploitation and aren't simply beneficiaries.

freedom-to-discriminate.reason: Businesses open to the public shouldn't be allowed to refuse people based on race, religion or similar traits.
